prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for every Atlanta home — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, the size/age of your house, your budget, and whether you want a high-efficiency system or a basic replacement. I can give a short list of well-regarded providers near you, but first it helps if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood.

Meanwhile, here’s how to pick the best company and what to expect:

What to ask and check
- Ask for 3 written estimates so you can compare scope and price.
- Require a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing), and ask for duct evaluation (leaks or needed repairs).
- Verify technicians are NATE-certified or similarly trained.
- Confirm the company is properly insured and registered to do business in Georgia.
- Request references and look at recent online reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB).
- Ask which brand and model they recommend, the unit’s SEER rating, and why.
- Get full written details: equipment specs, labor warranty, manufacturer warranty, permit pull, expected timeline, and cleanup.
- Ask whether they’ll match indoor/outdoor components and install a new thermostat if needed.
- Check if they offer financing, maintenance plans, and whether they’ll submit utility or manufacturer rebate paperwork.

Red flags
- No written estimate or vague scope of work.
- Pressuring you to replace when repairs or a tune-up might work.
- Extremely low bids without explanation (likely cut corners or hidden fees).
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.

Typical price ranges (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Basic AC replacement (straight swap, 2–3 ton): roughly $4,000–$8,000.
- High-efficiency systems, new ductwork, or complicated installs: $8,000–$15,000+.
(Prices vary by home size, SEER rating, refrigerant type, and duct/permit needs.)

Companies to consider
- Local authorized dealers of major brands (Carrier, Trane, Lennox) — factory dealers often have good training and warranty handling.
- Coolray (large Georgia-based HVAC service & installation company) — common in metro Atlanta.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (regional/national HVAC + plumbing service) — present in many metro areas and offers broad service options.

If you want, I can:
- Look up the top-rated HVAC installers in your ZIP code and give 3–5 vetted recommendations with review summaries; or
- Tell you exactly what questions to ask over the phone for a particular quote you received.

Which would you prefer? If you want local names, please share your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and any preferences (budget, brand, timeline).
